incident_details.title: High Risk Alerts: ESA for 192.168.10.205
incident_details.description: This is a network-only alert showing repeated outbound connections from internal host 192.168.10.205 to external IPs over HTTPS and DNS, including a high-risk destination. There is no endpoint, process, file, or PowerShell evidence to confirm compromise, so this is suspicious activity that warrants investigation rather than an immediate high-severity escalation.

gap_findings.step_3: Was any malicious process spawne: No process creation evidence is present in the incident data. The only concrete activity is a network egress session from 192.168.10.205:32946 to 34.107.243.93:443 (googleusercontent.com) flagged by 'Chu Wen - Lateral Move Detected.' Because the payload is only 28 bytes and there are no process names, parent/child references, command lines, hashes, or host telemetry, we cannot confirm a spawned malicious process from this dataset.
gap_findings.step_4: Analyze the process tree for sig: A process tree is not present in the incident data, so direct analysis is impossible. However, the alert title and network metadata suggest possible lateral movement rather than privilege escalation: the source IP is 192.168.10.205 and the destination is an external Google Cloud IP (34.107.243.93) over HTTPS, which is inconsistent with classic internal-to-internal lateral movement. The session is labeled 'data push' and 'not top 20 dst' with a very small payload, which could indicate beaconing or small-volume exfiltration, but there is no host process context to support that. No evidence of privilege escalation artifacts, spawned shells, service creation, or remote execution is visible here.
gap_findings.step_1: Identify 1. username 2. IP addre: IP address is directly present as 192.168.10.205. Username is not populated in the alert, but the NetWitness source trail includes 'admin2@192.168.20.14:50005', which strongly suggests an administrative user or analyst context associated with the session chain; this is likely the investigating/admin trail rather than the endpoint user, so confidence is limited. Login details are absent in the incident record (no logon type, time, source workstation, or authentication event). Computer name/host name is missing; only the IP and MAC address 00:0c:29:f3:50:e1 identify the endpoint. Operating system is not present; no OS metadata is populated in the alert.

actionable_queries.step_3: Was any malicious process spawne: Collect endpoint process telemetry from EDR or Windows Security log Event ID 4688 (Process Creation) on host 192.168.10.205 for the timeframe around 2025-07-15 08:56:46 UTC. If Sysmon is deployed, query Event ID 1 for process creation with parent/child chain, command line, and hashes. Recommended EDR search: host.ip=192.168.10.205 AND event.type=process AND @timestamp:[2025-07-15T08:45:00Z TO 2025-07-15T09:10:00Z].
actionable_queries.step_4: Analyze the process tree for sig: Pull the full process tree from EDR for host 192.168.10.205 around the alert time, including parent PID, child PID, command line, integrity level, token elevation, and signer. On Windows, query Security Event ID 4688, 4672 (Special Privileges Assigned), 4624/4634 (logon/logoff), 4697/7045 (service creation), 7040 (service change), 7045, and Sysmon Event IDs 1, 3, 7, 10, 11, 12, 13, 22. If remote execution is suspected, also query 5140/5145 (share access) and 7040/7045 for service-based lateral movement.
